Date: 2026-06-25
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes

summary: Kickoff for Riverside Health onboarding to Redwood. Covered scope of pilot, success metrics, security requirements (SAML, KMS, audit logs), deployment preference (start hosted, move to Dedicated/VPC for regulated data), and next steps for benchmarks and security deep-dive.
topics: Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, welcome to the Riverside + Redwood onboarding kickoff. I'm Jordan, AE. We've got Maya, our CSM, and Alex, our SE. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Elena (Riverside): Elena here. Hi.
[00:12] Tom (Riverside): Tom — hi all.
[00:14] Sara (Riverside): Sara, compliance.
[00:16] Luis (Riverside): Luis here.
[00:18] Jordan: Great. Agenda: scope of pilot, security requirements, deployment options, perf benchmarks, and next steps. We'll try to keep it to 45 minutes.
[00:30] Maya (Redwood CSM): I'll be your point for onboarding tasks and timelines, and we'll coordinate the pilot rollout.
[00:35] Alex (Redwood SE): I'll handle the technical benching and any integration questions.
[00:40] Tom: Quick context - we're looking to add LLM-powered triage and discharge summaries into our EHR flows. Primary concerns are latency (sub-300ms for short queries), PII handling, and cost predictability.
[00:55] Jordan: Perfect — that's consistent with other healthcare customers. For latency, we usually recommend starting hosted API to move fast and then plan a Dedicated or Private deployment once playbooks/prompt sets stabilize. Does that timeline sound right?
[01:10] Elena: Yes, but we have a compliance preference for data not to leave our VPC after initial pilot. So we need to understand VPC/on-prem options and KMS integration early.
[01:25] Sara: Also we need SOC2 evidence, audit logs, and a clear data retention policy. Who handles key management? We use Azure Key Vault.
[01:35] Maya: We have a Private deployment option with customer-managed KMS/HSM and can support Azure Key Vault integrations; I'll share the security pack after the call. We also have audit logs and long-term retention as an add-on.
[01:50] Alex: From a SE perspective, we can run an initial integration with sample prompts without sending PHI to hosted env — we can mask or synthetize the data. For the pilot, many teams start hosted for speed, then migrate to Dedicated or Private VPC when ready.
[02:10] Luis: Operationally, we'd want the option to pin model versions and control rollouts — can Redwood do canary/A-B rollouts and automatic fallback?
[02:20] Alex: Yes — rollout policies: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. You can pin versions in the config. We'll demo that in the next session.
[02:35] Tom: On cost — we care about predictable spend. How does Redwood's Dedicated pricing compare to hosted? And what about batching/quantization to reduce token costs?
[02:50] Jordan: Hosted is usage-based and great for dev. Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and cost efficiency at scale. We also have Optimize recommendations for batching, caching, and quantization profiles. Alex can outline recommended quant levels for your workload.
[03:10] Alex: For discharge summary style generation, a 4-bit quantized model on Dedicated often gives large cost savings with small quality delta depending on the model and prompt length. We can test quantization vs full precision in the benchmark.
[03:30] Sara: Important: encryption in transit and at rest, and separation between customer data sets. Also need RBAC and SSO for our admins.
[03:40] Maya: We support SAML SSO and RBAC. I'll include the SAML metadata exchange in the security email.
[03:48] Jordan: Let's map success criteria — what does Riverside need to call the pilot successful?
[03:55] Elena: Accuracy on key extraction for triage must be >= 92% on our holdout set. Latency under 300ms for queries under 200 tokens. Cost under $X per 1K summaries — we'll give exact target offline.
[04:10] Tom: Also we need reproducible evals and regression alerts. If a model update drops quality, we need automatic alerts tied to prompt tests.
[04:20] Alex: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to eval sets. We can onboard your prompt set and wire up alerts.
[04:30] Luis: For pilot traffic, we're expecting around 50k tokens/day initially. How will that map to Dedicated sizing?
[04:40] Alex: We'll benchmark with your sample sets. For 50k tokens/day, hosted will be fine initially, but dedicated sizing depends on concurrency and latency SLOs; I'll run a throughput vs latency matrix.
[05:00] Elena: One more — legal/procurement wants to know data residency — can you guarantee EU-only regions?
[05:10] Jordan: Yes, we have region controls and can deploy in specific cloud regions for residency. For Private deployments, it's customer-controlled.
[05:20] Sara: Please send SOC2 and encryption docs.
[05:22] Maya: Will do.
[05:25] [10:30] Alex: Quick note on integration patterns — we expose REST SDKs for generation, chat, embeddings. For EHR integration, many customers use a service side queue and prefix/KV caching to avoid repeat calls. Caching can reduce token usage dramatically.
[05:45] Luis: Do you have examples for prefix/KV cache and recommended TTLs?
[05:50] Alex: Yes, we'll include config examples in the quickstart repo. Typical TTLs vary, but for discharge templates you can cache fairly aggressively for repeated fragments.
[06:05] Tom: Are there any gotchas with our Kubernetes infra and the Redwood agent? We run on AKS.
[06:12] Alex: We support AKS — the Private package has an agent for on-prem/K8s integration. We'll provide manifests and a deployment checklist.
[06:25] Jordan: Ok big picture timeline proposal: this week — share keys/docs; next 1–2 weeks — run perf benchmark and security review; week 3 — pilot start in hosted; week 4 — review and plan Dedicated/VPC migration if needed. Sound reasonable?
[06:45] Elena: Yes.
[06:48] Sara: Yes, as long as security review is early.
[06:50] Maya: We'll prioritize that.
[07:00] [15:00] Jordan: Any blockers or open questions we should capture?
[07:05] Luis: Need to validate Azure Key Vault integration and any latency implications.
[07:10] Alex: We'll put a test plan for KMS calls and measure.
[07:15] Tom: Can you share a sample benchmark spreadsheet?
[07:18] Jordan: Yes — sending after call.
[07:20] Elena: Also would like to see a short runbook for rollback if a model causes hallucinations in summarization.
[07:30] Alex: We'll draft a rollback/playbook with canary thresholds and automatic fallback rules.
[07:40] [30:00] Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps — Jordan will send the onboarding deck, Alex will run perf tests and share results, Maya will schedule security deep dive and send SOC2/KMS docs, Luis will provide prompt set and metrics.
[07:55] Elena: Who's the contact for legal/procurement questions?
[08:00] Jordan: I'll loop in our legal rep but Maya will coordinate procurement docs.
[08:10] Sara: Please include data processing addendum and PII handling details.
[08:15] Maya: Noted.
[08:20] Jordan: Anything else?
[08:25] Tom: No from me.
[08:27] Luis: All good.
[08:30] Jordan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the security deep-dive for the week of 2026-07-06. Meeting adjourned.
[08:40] [End 45:00]
